original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Health authorities are racing to trace dozens of people who disembarked from a hantavirus-hit cruise ship on the island of St Helena in the South Atlantic.

The ship's operator said 29 passengers, of at least 12 different nationalities, left the MV Hondius on 24 April. The Dutch government gave a different figure of 40.

Among those who left the Dutch vessel at the island was a 69-year-old woman who later died in South Africa.

The Dutch government said a Swiss national who has since been diagnosed with hantavirus was also one of those who left the cruise at the British Overseas Territory.

Two other people died on board the ship, which set sail from Argentina a month ago.

Three others were evacuated from the ship on Wednesday, of British, Dutch and German nationalities.

The British man has been named as 56-year-old Martin Anstee and is in a stable condition. The other evacuees were a 41-year-old Dutch crew member and a 65-year-old German, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

Oceanwide Expeditions said in an update on Thursday that 30 people, including the body of one of the guests who died, had disembarked on 24 April.

This included seven British people and six Americans, as well as guests from countries including Canada, Germany, Singapore, Turkey and Switzerland.

It added that the first confirmed case of hantavirus was not reported until 4 May and that all guests who disembarked the ship have been contacted by it.

Oceanwide Expeditions also said it remained in "close and continual discussion with relevant authorities regarding our exact point of arrival, quarantine and screening procedures for all guests".

The Dutch luxury cruise liner is set to dock in Spain's Canary Islands in the coming days.

The WHO has said eight cases of hantavirus - three confirmed and five suspected - have so far been identified in people who were on board.

Officials have said that one of the deceased had the virus, while the other two deaths are under investigation.

The Dutch government said the ship stopped at St Helena on its way to Cape Verde, an archipelago nation off the West African coast.

Among those who disembarked was a 69-year-old Dutch woman who left the cruise at St Helena on 24 April, and travelled to South Africa, where she died two days later. Her husband died on board the cruise on 11 April, but is not a confirmed case of hantavirus.

The Dutch government update said before her death she had boarded a KLM flight heading from Johannesburg 

---

[Lähde: NPR]
The MV Hondius cruise ship departs the port in Praia, Cape Verde, Wednesday, May 6, 2026.
                
                    
                    Misper Apawu/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

THE HAGUE, Netherlands — About 40 passengers on a cruise ship hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak previously disembarked on the remote South Atlantic island of St. Helena after the first passenger died, Dutch officials said Thursday.

The dozens of passengers, including the wife of a Dutch man who died, left the cruise ship during a stop at the British territory, the Dutch foreign ministry said.

The Dutch cruise company that operates the ship previously said the Dutch woman disembarked the ship with her husband's body at St. Helena. She then flew to South Africa on a commercial plane and died after collapsing at an airport in Johannesburg.

However, the company had not acknowledged that anyone else got off the ship at St. Helena.

Authorities in South Africa and Europe are trying to trace contacts of any passengers who got off the ship. It emerged Wednesday that a man tested positive for hantavirus in Switzerland after he also disembarked at St. Helena and flew home, though his precise movements aren't clear.

Dutch authorities did not confirm where other passengers who disembarked are now.

A British man was evacuated from the ship to South Africa from Ascension Island days later, according to the company, while three people, including the ship's doctor, were evacuated from the ship while it was near Cape Verde and taken to Europe for treatment on Wednesday.

Three passengers have died in the outbreak, and several others are sick.

---

[Lähde: ABC7 News]
The hantavirus-hit cruise ship MV Hondius on Thursday is en route to Spain's Canary Islands, as European and African authorities rush to trace anyone who may have come into contact with the virus.

The journey from the archipelago nation off Africa's west coast to the island of Tenerife, one of the Canary Islands, is expected to take three and a half days, the Spanish Ministry of Health told CNN Wednesday.

The ship's departure came soon after three people were evacuated from the vessel.

Two of them have landed in Amsterdam where they have been received by specialist medical teams, according to the cruise ship operator Oceanwide Expeditions.

The plane carrying the third patient had to make an unscheduled landing at Gran Canaria Airport, in the Canary Islands, to refuel after being refused permission to do so in Morocco. A malfunction with the patient's medical equipment caused further delays, a source at the ministry said.

"The patient does not pose a risk to public health and will remain on the runway until the situation is resolved," the source said.

Another passenger previously on board the MV Hondius tested positive for hantavirus and is being treated at a Swiss hospital, Switzerland's health ministry said Wednesday. That takes the total tally to eight cases of hantavirus - three confirmed and five suspected. Three people have died in the suspected outbreak and several others have fallen ill.

Meanwhile, local politicians are wrangling over the plan for the ship to dock in the Canary Islands.

payload.title: Viranomaiset jäljittävät hantavirukselle mahdollisesti altistuneita risteilymatkustajia
payload.summary: Etelä-Afrikan ja Euroopan viranomaiset selvittävät, keihin MV Hondius -aluksesta St Helenalla poistuneet matkustajat ovat olleet yhteydessä hantavirusryppään jälkeen.
payload.content:
Etelä-Afrikan ja Euroopan viranomaiset yrittävät jäljittää yhteyksiä matkustajiin, jotka poistuivat MV Hondius -risteilyalukselta St Helenan saarella sen jälkeen, kun aluksella oli kuollut matkustaja. Noin 40 ihmisen kerrotaan poistuneen aluksesta syrjäisellä Etelä-Atlantin saarella, ja joukossa oli 69-vuotias hollantilaisnainen, joka matkusti myöhemmin Etelä-Afrikkaan ja kuoli kaksi päivää St Helenalta lähtönsä jälkeen.

## Matkustajia poistui St Helenalla

Hollantilaisviranomaisten mukaan noin 40 matkustajaa poistui risteilyalukselta St Helenalla sen jälkeen, kun ensimmäinen matkustaja oli kuollut. Alus on yhdistetty kuolemaan johtaneeseen hantavirusryppääseen, minkä vuoksi viranomaiset selvittävät nyt mahdollisia altistumisia ja matkustajien myöhempiä kontakteja. Lähdetietojen perusteella kyse ei ole vain aluksella olleiden ihmisten tilanteen arvioinnista, vaan myös siitä, keitä maihin nousseet matkustajat ovat voineet tavata jatkomatkoillaan.

Tapauksen keskiössä on 69-vuotias hollantilaisnainen, joka poistui risteilyltä St Helenalla 24. huhtikuuta. Hän matkusti saarelta Etelä-Afrikkaan, missä hän kuoli kaksi päivää myöhemmin. Naisen puoliso oli kuollut aluksella 11. huhtikuuta, mutta hänen kuolemaansa ei ole vahvistettu hantavirustapaukseksi. Tämä ero on olennainen, koska viranomaiset ovat vahvistaneet vain rajallisen määrän yksityiskohtia sairastumisista ja kuolinsyistä.

## Selvitys ulottuu useisiin maihin

Viranomaiset Etelä-Afrikassa ja Euroopassa pyrkivät tavoittamaan henkilöitä, jotka ovat voineet olla tekemisissä alukselta poistuneiden matkustajien kanssa. Selvitystyötä vaikeuttaa se, että matkustajat ovat jatkaneet matkaansa eri suuntiin saarelta poistumisen jälkeen. St Helena sijaitsee kaukana Etelä-Atlantilla, mutta sieltä lähteneiden matkustajien myöhemmät reitit voivat ulottua useisiin maihin.

Tapaus sai lisää huomiota, kun ilmeni, että Sveitsissä miehellä todettiin hantavirus sen jälkeen, kun hän oli myös poistunut alukselta St Helenalla ja lentänyt kotiin. Hänen tarkkoja liikkeitään ei ole kerrottu selvästi. Tämän vuoksi kontaktien jäljitys nojaa saatavilla oleviin matkustustietoihin ja viranomaisten väliseen tiedonvaihtoon.

## Vahvistettuja tietoja on rajallisesti

Hantavirukset voivat aiheuttaa ihmisille vakavia sairauksia, mutta tämän tapauksen yksityiskohdista on julkisuudessa vahvistettu vain rajallinen määrä tietoja. Saatavilla olevien tietojen mukaan viranomaisten ensisijainen tavoite on selvittää mahdolliset altistumisketjut ja ehkäistä lisätartuntoja, jos sellaisia on tapahtunut. Samalla tapaukseen liittyy yhä avoimia kysymyksiä, kuten kaikkien alukselta poistuneiden matkustajien myöhemmät kontaktit ja tarkat liikkeet.

Yksi poistuneista oli 69-vuotias hollantilaisnainen, joka kuoli myöhemmin Etelä-Afrikassa.
Etelä-Afrikan ja Euroopan viranomaiset jäljittävät matkustajien mahdollisia kontakteja.
